page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps. The system runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 384.64 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 170.56 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21489.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 46924.96, both placing in the top tier. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware AES acceleration, though the ARM architecture lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX-512. Large-scale LLM inference on a 70B model represents a performance tradeoff, yielding a weaker prompt processing speed of 5.91 tokens/sec.

The instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from local, high-speed NVMe storage. The combination of dedicated ARMv9 cores and high-throughput memory bandwidth makes it highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and static web serving. It is less suited for workloads requiring specialized GPU acceleration or x86 instruction sets.
